display_name: Legislate a primary or principal role
description: Fleet session-management D4 (Part B item 1; §3.1 Q1). The ONE sanctioned governance-act path that stamps an authority-carrying role_class ('primary' or 'principal') onto a role row at birth. peer_claim_role's claim-time gate is enforce-by-class only — a fresh mint always stamps the project default and structurally cannot assign primary/principal — so this verb is the sole place class-assignment happens. A 'primary'-class name must match the reserved <solet>-Main pattern the mint-refusal guard protects (e.g. 'Coordinator-Main'); 'project'/'ephemeral'/'chat' are refused outright (role_class_not_legislatable) since those are minted by a claim or a spawn, never legislated. The write is a race-safe INSERT-only first-write (on_conflict=do_nothing): a fresh name is legislated; a re-run naming the SAME class already on record is an idempotent no-op ('already_legislated'); a re-run naming a DIFFERENT class is refused loud (role_class_conflict), never silently reassigned. directed_by is server-built from call_context (the same provenance convention spawn_session uses) — never caller-supplied.
embedding_description: Legislate (create) a role row with role_class primary or principal, the governance act that makes a reserved <solet>-Main seat or a principal office claimable — distinct from peer_claim_role (which only ever claims an EXISTING role and can never assign its class) and from spawn_session (which mints project/ephemeral roles, never primary/principal ones).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: action ('legislated' on a fresh row, 'already_legislated' on an idempotent re-run naming the same class already on record), name (the legislated role name), and role_class (the class actually on record — always echoes what was requested, since a mismatch is refused rather than returned).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: State which role was legislated under which class, and whether this was a fresh legislation or a no-op re-run of an already-legislated row. This verb only creates the row — it never claims the role for any session; a claim (peer_claim_role / /rename) is a separate, later act.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: All validation runs BEFORE the state write, so a refused call never touches state. missing_argument and role_class_not_legislatable are argument-shape checks; reserved_primary_name_required and role_class_conflict are policy refusals evaluated against the requested name/class and (for the conflict case) the existing row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: name or brief_ref was empty. role_class_not_legislatable: role_class was not 'primary' or 'principal' — project/ephemeral/chat roles are minted, never legislated, through this verb. reserved_primary_name_required: role_class='primary' was requested for a name that does not match the reserved <solet>-Main pattern, so the mint-refusal guard was never protecting it. role_class_conflict: the role row already exists with a DIFFERENT role_class than requested — never silently reassigned. state_service_unavailable: state_service is not bound on this solet.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For role_class_not_legislatable, use peer_claim_role (project) or spawn_session (ephemeral/project/principal-fill) instead — this verb is not the mint path. For reserved_primary_name_required, either rename the target to the <solet>-Main shape or legislate it as role_class='principal' instead. For role_class_conflict, confirm which class is actually intended for that name; legislating a different class on an existing row is a distinct operator decision, never automatic here.
